title: Limits
mcqIntro: 12 quick concept checks — two for each of the module's six sections, built from the traps the notes flag rather than from the routine drills. Pick an answer to check it instantly; a wrong pick names the specific misreading it comes from and points you at the section to re-read. The real work of the module is in the 14 written problems below.

mcq.stem: A student writes the difference quotient for $f(x)=x^2$ at $x=3$, substitutes $h=0$ straight away, and lands on $\dfrac{0}{0}$. What has that result actually told them?

options.a: the tangent slope at that point is equal to zero
options.b: the curve fails to have a tangent there
options.c: the algebra needs simplifying before $h$ shrinks
options.d: the secant slope is undefined at each step $h$

mcq.stem: At the point $(2,5)$ on a curve, the tangent line has slope $4$. The normal line at that same point has slope
Inside $\dfrac{x+3}{x+5}$ a student crosses the $x$ on top against the $x$ underneath. What makes that step illegal?

options.a: cancelling needs equal constants above and below
options.b: each $x$ carries a hidden sign in front of it
options.c: each $x$ sits inside a sum, so it is not a factor
options.d: the fraction has to be rationalised beforehand

mcq.stem: Putting $x=3$ into $\dfrac{x^2-x-6}{x-3}$ returns $\dfrac{0}{0}$. Which conclusion follows?

options.a: the limit fails to exist at $x=3$
options.c: the limit runs off to infinity there

mcq.stem: In the tolerance game behind $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to a}f(x)=L$, what is it that $\varepsilon$ measures?

options.b: how steep the graph is near $a$

mcq.stem: For $f(x)=6x$ near $a=1$ the shortcut $\delta=\varepsilon/|m|$ hands back $\delta=0.05$. A classmate works with $\delta=0.02$ instead. That choice is

options.a: wrong, since the formula fixes delta exactly
options.b: wrong, since delta has to exceed epsilon
options.c: sound, since a tighter input window still works
options.d: sound, provided epsilon is doubled to match

mcq.stem: Both one-sided limits of a piecewise $f$ at $x=1$ come out as $4$, yet the rule assigns $f(1)=7$. The value of $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to 1}f(x)$ is then

options.a: $7$, since the assigned value wins at $x=1$
options.b: $4$, but the point needs redefining first
options.d: $4$, since a limit ignores the assigned value

mcq.stem: Describe how $g(x)=\dfrac{|x-6|}{x-6}$ behaves on each side of $x=6$.

options.a: zero from both sides, so the limit is zero
options.b: minus one from the left, plus one from the right
options.c: plus one from both sides, so the limit is one
options.d: plus one from the left, minus one from the right

mcq.stem: A function has matching one-sided limits of $3$ at $x=2$, while its rule sets $f(2)=8$. Which description fits the graph there?

options.a: fully continuous, since the two sides agree
options.b: a removable discontinuity, a hole to patch
options.c: a jump discontinuity, with the sides at odds
options.d: an infinite discontinuity, a vertical blowup

mcq.stem: The rule $f(x)=x^2+1$ for $x<2$ and $f(x)=kx-3$ for $x\ge 2$ turns out to be continuous at $x=2$ when $k$ takes the value
The graph of $y=\dfrac{(x-5)(x+2)}{(x-5)(x-1)}$ runs into trouble at $x=5$. What sits at that input?

options.a: a removable hole, because that factor cancels
options.b: a vertical asymptote, because the bottom vanishes
options.c: a horizontal asymptote at that same height
options.d: an ordinary point where the graph stays smooth

mcq.stem: Which line does the graph of $y=\dfrac{6x^2-x+4}{2x^2+9}$ flatten toward far out to the right?

short.prompt: Let $f(x)=3x^2-4x$. Work through the difference quotient $\dfrac{f(1+h)-f(1)}{h}$, simplify it completely, then let $h\to 0$ to obtain the slope of the tangent at $x=1$. Show the step where the $h$ is cancelled. [3 marks]

A drone is launched so that its height in metres after $t$ seconds is $H(t)=24t-4t^2$. Find its average velocity over the interval from $t=1$ to $t=4$, and say in one sentence what that number describes about the flight. [3 marks]
Evaluate $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to 5}\frac{x^2-3x-10}{x-5}$. Begin by recording what direct substitution produces, then repair it. [3 marks]
A workshop's revenue in dollars from selling $x$ chairs is $R(x)=8x-0.02x^2$. Compute $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to 20}R(x)$, and explain why no algebraic repair is called for here. [3 marks]

For $f(x)=5x-2$ approaching $a=3$, the target is $L=13$ and the output must stay within $\varepsilon=0.35$ of $L$. Produce a delta that guarantees this, then confirm the guarantee by testing the two edge inputs. [3 marks]
Take $f(x)=4x+5$ for $x\le -1$ and $f(x)=-2x$ for $x>-1$. Work out each one-sided limit at $x=-1$ and decide whether $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to -1}f(x)$ exists. [3 marks]

A left-luggage locker charges $L(h)=6$ dollars for $0<h\le 2$ and $L(h)=10$ dollars for $2<h\le 4$. Find the two one-sided limits at $h=2$, and say what a customer experiences the moment the clock passes two hours. [3 marks]
Find the number $b$ for which $f(x)=2x+b$ on $x\le 4$ and $f(x)=x^2-5$ on $x>4$ is continuous at $x=4$. State which of the three continuity conditions your equation is enforcing. [3 marks]
Locate the vertical asymptotes of $y=\dfrac{3x}{x^2-2x-8}$, and justify why each one is genuine rather than a hole. [3 marks]

A print shop's average cost per poster is $A(x)=\dfrac{800+4x}{x}$ dollars when $x$ posters are produced. Find the horizontal asymptote as $x\to\infty$, and explain in the language of fixed and variable cost what the shop should read into it. [3 marks]

extended.title: A cyclist on a straight road
extended.intro: A cyclist's distance from a lamp post, in metres, $t$ seconds after she sets off is modelled by $s(t)=t^2+6t$ for $0\le t\le 6$. Throughout this question work from the limit definition only — no differentiation rules have been introduced yet.

parts.prompt: Find the cyclist's average velocity over the interval from $t=0$ to $t=4$, and name the line on the distance-time graph whose slope that number is. [2 marks]
Using $\displaystyle\lim_{k\to 0}\frac{s(2+k)-s(2)}{k}$, obtain her instantaneous velocity at $t=2$. Expand every bracket before cancelling anything. [3 marks]
Write the equation of the tangent line to the graph of $s$ at $t=2$, and then the equation of the normal line at that same point. [3 marks]

The cyclist claims: *'my average speed over the first four seconds was the same as my speed at $t=2$.'* Using your answers above, say whether the numbers support her, and explain in one sentence why the agreement is a feature of this particular model rather than a general law. [2 marks]

extended.title: Two models that break at a single point
extended.intro: An engineer is handed two formulas, each of which misbehaves at exactly one input. Neither model is useless — each simply needs some algebra before it will give up its value.

parts.prompt: The first model is $v(t)=\dfrac{t^2-25}{t-5}$, the speed of a trolley in metres per second for $t$ near $5$. Record what direct substitution returns, and explain in one sentence why that result is not the answer. [2 marks]
Evaluate $\displaystyle\lim_{t\to 5}v(t)$ by factoring, and state the speed the trolley is heading toward even though the formula yields nothing at $t=5$ itself. [3 marks]

The second model is $w(x)=\dfrac{\sqrt{x+25}-5}{x}$ for $x$ near $0$, where factoring is of no help. Carry out the appropriate rationalising step and evaluate $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to 0}w(x)$. [3 marks]
Each of your two answers is a number the formula itself never produces. Explain what that reveals about the difference between a limit and a function value. [2 marks]

extended.title: A courier's pricing table
extended.intro: A courier charges $C(w)=7+3w$ dollars for a parcel weighing $w$ kilograms up to and including $5$ kg, and $C(w)=q+5w$ dollars for anything heavier. The company wants no visible step in the price at the $5$ kg mark.

parts.prompt: Leaving $q$ as an unknown, write down $\displaystyle\lim_{w\to 5^-}C(w)$ and $\displaystyle\lim_{w\to 5^+}C(w)$. [2 marks]
Determine the value of $q$ that removes the step, and name which of the three continuity conditions your equation is enforcing. [3 marks]
A rival courier sets $q=0$ instead. Classify the discontinuity that appears at $w=5$, and state how much a customer's bill changes across that instant. [3 marks]
Explain why confirming that the two one-sided limits agree would not, on its own, prove the price function is continuous at $w=5$. [2 marks]

extended.title: Reading a reaction-rate curve
extended.intro: A chemist models the rate of a reaction, in units per second, as $r(c)=\dfrac{4c^2-16}{c^2-c-2}$, where $c$ is the concentration of a reagent. She wants to know the curve's long-run height and exactly where it breaks down.

parts.prompt: Factor the numerator and the denominator completely, then cancel whatever the two share. [2 marks]
Identify the vertical asymptote and the removable hole, making clear which input gives which and on what grounds. [3 marks]
Find the horizontal asymptote as $c\to\infty$, and state what it tells the chemist about the rate at high concentration. [3 marks]
As $c$ approaches $-1$ from the right, does $r$ run off to $+\infty$ or to $-\infty$? Justify your answer using the sign of each factor. [2 marks]
